newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania to avoid firm leu, plans C/A convertibility.
newsitem.headline: Romania to avoid firm leu, plans C/A convertibility.

text.p: Top Romanian officials pledged on Thursday to keep the leu from strengthening as part of an overall efforts to help economic recovery and achieve current account convertibility.

Central bank (BNR) governor Mugur Isarescu said a stronger leu was not beneficial for the economy after the currency's stabilisation in recent months near 7,500 to the dollar after plunging to a record low of about 9,000 in earlier this year.

"Romania's economy cannot afford a stronger leu," Isarescu told a news conference alongside Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea at the close of a month-long International Monetary Fund mission assessing the state of Romania's reforms.

Ciorbea, who heads the centrist coalition government which took office last year after seven years of leftist rule, said plans to achieve current account convertibility would be complete by September.
"By the end of August or no later than September, we will remove all the obstacles," he said. "This is an important achievement which will boost Romania's credibility."

Romania has limited current account convertibility and the leu floats freely without corridors. Firms buy and sell hard currency freely for current account operations, but individuals are entitled to buy only the equivalent of $500 per year.
Analysts said reining in any leu upswing, which could later unleash an equally strong downward push, was vital to keep control over inflation and budget and trade deficits.
Monthly inflation is expected to stand at between one and 1.5 percent in July, down from a record 30.7 percent in March. The January-May trade gap was nearly half the same 1996 figure.

As monthly inflation is expected to stay below two percent until the end of the year, officials say Romania should ease monetary policies to boost recovery after months of constraints sent interest rates up to 200 percent earlier this year.
But officials said any easing had to be cautious to preserve confidence in the currency.

"The central bank is now facing the difficult task of having to ease monetary policy somewhat," the IMF's chief negotiator for Romania, Poul Thomsen, said in an interview. "There are signs that there is scope for easing monetary policy. But how much? Very cautious, gradual."

Liberalisation of markets, investor-friendly legislation and pledges of faster reform produced large foreign capital inflows. That prompted BNR intervention in recent months to counter upward pressure on the leu.

BNR dollar purchases flooded the market with leu funds, depressing money market rates, now at 30 percent. But it has also build up foreign reserves, now at $2 billion and seen rising to $3 billion or even $4 billion by end of the year.
Analysts and traders have said that a gradual slide for the currency would help exporters and ensure an economic recovery on a sound basis of export-led growth.

Although most of Romania's trading partners are in the European Union, most deals are conducted in dollars. On Thursday, the leu closed slightly firmer, quoted at around 7,425/525 to the dollar against an opening of 7,450/550.
